mentions.name: D&D Telepresence Robot
mentions.description: A telepresence robot for joining in-person D&D sessions remotely. It is built around a Raspberry Pi driving two microphones and servos, with 3D printed parts on a lazy susan base that lets the body rotate and the head tilt up and down, so the binaural microphones can be aimed at whoever is speaking. This helps the remote player clearly hear individual speakers such as the DM during busy table conversations. Development is currently paused on a PWM controller detection issue after rewiring the cable layout.
mentions.problem: The builder is often the only remote participant in D&D sessions, and it is difficult to hear just the DM talk when everyone else at the table is talking.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm getting out of my comfort zone (software) to work on a telepresence robot for my D&D games.  My main motivator for this is that I'm often the only person remote for these sessions and it's difficult to hear just the DM talk when everyone else is talking.
mentions.author: philote
